concepts.def: Dynastic civil wars between the houses of Lancaster and York for the English crown, weakening the nobility and paving the way for Tudor rule.
Henry Tudor's defeat and killing of Richard III, ending the Wars of the Roses and founding the Tudor dynasty as Henry VII.
A royal prerogative court strengthened under the early Tudors to enforce order over overmighty subjects and bypass the slower common-law courts.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Crown, Parliament & People 1455-1556 — a core area of A-Level History.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Crown, Parliament & People 1455-1556 brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Crown, Parliament & People 1455-1556.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which 1485 battle founded the Tudor dynasty?
options: Bosworth
Towton
Tewkesbury
Flodden

mcqs.q: What did the Reformation Parliament of 1529-36 establish?
options: Royal supremacy over the Church
The end of the monarchy
A republic
The Magna Carta

mcqs.q: What did the Wars of the Roses fight over?
options: The English crown between Lancaster and York
Control of France
Religious freedom
The right to vote

mcqs.q: What did Henry VIII gain from the Dissolution of the Monasteries?
options: Their wealth and lands
A new parliament
Control of Scotland
Papal approval

mcqs.q: Did the Reformation Parliament make England Protestant?
options: The Reformation Parliament abolished the monarchy.
Henry VIII turned England fully Protestant in the 1530s.
It broke with Rome and made the king head of the Church, but Henry VIII's England kept largely Catholic doctrine and worship.
Parliament chose who became king.

mcqs.q: How strong was the crown after Bosworth in 1485?
options: The Reformation Parliament abolished the monarchy.
Henry VII secured the throne but faced pretenders and overmighty nobles, working steadily to bolster royal finances and control.
Henry VII ruled jointly with Parliament as equals.
Henry VII was instantly secure with no challenges after 1485.

mcqs.q: What was Parliament's role under the early Tudors?
options: Parliament met regularly and limited the crown like a modern legislature.
Parliament was summoned by the monarch and used to legitimise major change, such as the break with Rome, not as a permanent independent body.
Parliament chose who became king.
Henry VII ruled jointly with Parliament as equals.
